facts.one_liner: César Ritz’s Piccadilly palace—the hotel that gave English the word “ritzy”.
facts.why_go: Opened by Swiss hotelier César Ritz in 1906, The Ritz overlooks Green Park with a Parisian-style façade crowned by green copper lions, the hotel’s emblem. Its Louis XVI interiors have been called one of the all-time masterpieces of hotel architecture, and afternoon tea in the gilded Palm Court is a London institution. With only 111 rooms and 25 suites, it still feels like a private grand house.
facts.best_time: Year-round; book Palm Court afternoon tea weeks ahead, especially around Christmas.
facts.how_to_get_there: At 150 Piccadilly, directly above Green Park Underground station (Jubilee, Piccadilly and Victoria lines). Heathrow is about 45 minutes by taxi or via the Piccadilly line.
facts.good_to_know: A formal dress code applies in the Palm Court and restaurant—jackets and ties for gentlemen; no jeans or trainers.

facts.one_liner: The Place Vendôme legend where Hemingway drank and Coco Chanel lived for decades.
facts.why_go: César Ritz and chef Auguste Escoffier opened the Ritz in 1898 behind the 18th-century façade of a Place Vendôme townhouse designed by Jules Hardouin-Mansart. It was among the first hotels in Europe with en-suite bathrooms and electricity in every room. Suites are named after famous guests such as Coco Chanel, Bar Hemingway honours its most devoted drinker, and the Suite Impériale is listed as a French national monument.
facts.best_time: Spring and autumn are loveliest in Paris; Fashion Weeks (late Feb–Mar, late Sep–Oct) book out early.
facts.how_to_get_there: 15 Place Vendôme, 1st arrondissement; Métro Opéra, Madeleine or Tuileries are a short walk. CDG airport is about 45–60 minutes by car.
facts.good_to_know: Bar Hemingway is tiny and doesn’t take reservations—arrive early in the evening.

facts.one_liner: A Riviera icon where a seawater pool is cut into the rocks above the Mediterranean.
facts.why_go: Built in 1870 as the Villa Soleil and opened as a hotel in 1889, the Hôtel du Cap sits in pine gardens on the tip of Cap d’Antibes. A long avenue leads down to the Eden Roc pavilion and its famous seawater pool blasted into the cliffs. F. Scott Fitzgerald fictionalised it in Tender Is the Night, and it has been a hideaway for film stars during the Cannes Film Festival for generations.
facts.best_time: Seasonal—usually open mid-April to mid-October; May (Cannes Film Festival) and July–August are peak.
facts.how_to_get_there: On Boulevard J.F. Kennedy, Antibes. Nice Côte d’Azur Airport is about 30 minutes by car; Cannes is 20 minutes west.
facts.good_to_know: Swimming from the rocks and the Eden Roc pool is a highlight—book a cabana early in summer.

facts.one_liner: A 1910 Art Nouveau palace facing Bellagio across Lake Como, with a pool that floats on the lake.
facts.why_go: Built between 1908 and 1910 by Enea Gandola, Grand Hotel Tremezzo is an Art Nouveau landmark on Lake Como’s western shore, looking straight across the water to the Bellagio promontory. Its terraces, lemon-scented gardens and floating swimming pool on the lake make it one of the most photographed hotels in Italy, and the neighbouring Villa Carlotta gardens are a short stroll away.
facts.best_time: April–October (the hotel is seasonal); May and September are calm and warm.
facts.how_to_get_there: On the Via Regina in Tremezzina, about 1 hour 15 minutes by car from Milan Malpensa or Linate; public ferries stop in Tremezzo and link to Bellagio and Varenna.
facts.good_to_know: The hotel’s own boats run guests across the lake—book a sunset ride to Bellagio.

facts.one_liner: A 14th-century Doge’s family palazzo on the Venetian lagoon, steps from St Mark’s.
facts.why_go: The Danieli’s central wing was built as Palazzo Dandolo at the end of the 14th century, and it has welcomed travellers since the 1820s. Behind its rose-coloured Gothic façade on the Riva degli Schiavoni lies a gilded staircase hall that is one of Venice’s great interiors. The rooftop terrace looks over the lagoon to San Giorgio Maggiore. Now run by Four Seasons as The Danieli, Venezia, it counted Charles Dickens and Richard Wagner among its guests.
facts.best_time: April–June and September–October; winter brings mist, fewer crowds and occasional acqua alta.
facts.how_to_get_there: Next to the Doge’s Palace on the Riva degli Schiavoni; the San Zaccaria vaporetto stop is outside. Water taxis run from Marco Polo Airport in about 30 minutes.
facts.good_to_know: Even if not staying, the rooftop terrace is a memorable spot for a drink over the lagoon.

facts.why_go: The Palazzo Pisani Gritti was the 16th-century residence of Doge Andrea Gritti and sits on the Grand Canal directly opposite the dome of Santa Maria della Salute. Ernest Hemingway was a regular, and today its canal-side terrace is one of the most romantic places in Venice for an aperitivo as gondolas and vaporetti glide by.
facts.best_time: April–June and September–October.
facts.how_to_get_there: Campo Santa Maria del Giglio, San Marco; vaporetto line 1 stops at Santa Maria del Giglio next door. Water taxis from the airport pull up at the hotel’s own landing.
facts.good_to_know: A traghetto gondola crosses the Grand Canal from the hotel’s campo to the Salute side—a classic Venetian shortcut.

facts.one_liner: The “Pink Palace” on Sunset Boulevard—Hollywood’s favourite hideaway since 1912.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1912, before Beverly Hills was even a city, this Mediterranean Revival hotel was painted its signature pink in 1948. Its Polo Lounge hosted the Rat Pack, Humphrey Bogart and Marlene Dietrich, and its 23 garden bungalows have sheltered Elizabeth Taylor and Marilyn Monroe. The hotel appears on the cover of the Eagles’ Hotel California album and is the city’s first historic landmark.
facts.best_time: Year-round; spring and autumn are sunny and mild, and awards season (Jan–Mar) is its most glamorous.
facts.how_to_get_there: 9641 Sunset Boulevard; LAX airport is about 30–45 minutes by car depending on traffic.
facts.good_to_know: The banana-leaf wallpaper of the Fountain Coffee Room counter has barely changed since 1949.

facts.one_liner: A red-roofed Victorian seaside palace on one of America’s best beaches.
facts.why_go: When “The Del” opened in 1888 it was the largest resort hotel in the world. It is a rare surviving wooden Victorian beach resort—a National Historic Landmark with red turrets rising above a wide sandy Pacific beach. Presidents, royalty and Marilyn Monroe (who filmed Some Like It Hot here) have all stayed, and a skating rink on the beach-front terrace is a Christmas tradition.
facts.best_time: Year-round; summer is busiest, while autumn has warm water and fewer crowds.
facts.how_to_get_there: 1500 Orange Avenue, Coronado, across the bay from downtown San Diego—about 15 minutes by car from San Diego International Airport, or by ferry to Coronado.
facts.good_to_know: Walk the beach at sunset—the hotel’s towers glow pink and Coronado Beach is routinely ranked among the best in the US.

facts.one_liner: A railway castle on the shore of turquoise Lake Louise, under the Victoria Glacier.
facts.why_go: Developed by the Canadian Pacific Railway at the turn of the 20th century, the Chateau sits on the eastern shore of Lake Louise, whose glacial silt turns the water an unreal turquoise beneath the Victoria Glacier. Summer means canoeing on the lake and hiking to the Lake Agnes Tea House; winter brings a skating rink on the frozen lake and ice sculptures.
facts.best_time: June–September for hiking and canoeing; January–March for lake skating and skiing at Lake Louise Ski Resort.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 2 hours by car from Calgary International Airport via the Trans-Canada Highway; parking at the lake is limited, so shuttles run in summer.
facts.good_to_know: A Parks Canada pass is required to stay in Banff National Park; guests have their own parking at the hotel.

Its central red dome, cantilevered staircase and sea-facing rooms over the harbour make it the flagship of Taj Hotels, and its Sea Lounge has been Mumbai’s favourite meeting place for generations.

facts.why_go: Built of white marble around 1743–1746 by Maharana Jagat Singh II as a summer retreat for the Mewar royal family, the Jag Niwas palace covers an entire island on Lake Pichola. Reached only by boat, it looks across the water to Udaipur’s City Palace and the Aravalli hills, and it famously starred in the James Bond film Octopussy.
facts.best_time: October–March, when days are warm and dry; the lake is fullest after the monsoon.

facts.good_to_know: Only hotel guests and diners with reservations can visit the island—book a meal if you aren’t staying.

facts.why_go: Built in 1835 as a garden retreat and later expanded into the principal residence of Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II, Rambagh Palace became India’s first palace hotel after independence and has been run by Taj since 1972. Peacocks strut across the Mughal gardens, and the Polo Bar and marble verandas recall its royal past. It is often called the “Jewel of Jaipur”.

facts.how_to_get_there: On Bhawani Singh Road, about 20 minutes by car from Jaipur International Airport and 15 minutes from the walled Pink City.
facts.good_to_know: The hotel arranges vintage car rides and visits to the Amber Fort, about 40 minutes away.

facts.one_liner: A two-island Maldives resort famous for dining and sleeping beneath the sea.
facts.why_go: Spread across two islands linked by a 500-metre bridge in Alif Dhaal Atoll, the Conrad Maldives Rangali Island pioneered undersea hospitality: Ithaa, which opened in 2005, was described as the world’s first undersea restaurant, set 5 metres down in an acrylic tunnel among the reef fish. facts.how_to_get_there: About 30 minutes by seaplane from Velana International Airport in Malé.

facts.one_liner: A former khedive’s hunting lodge with the Great Pyramid filling the view.
facts.why_go: Built in 1869 as a hunting lodge for Khedive Isma’il Pasha and opened as a hotel in 1886, Mena House stands at the foot of the Giza plateau—many rooms and its gardens look straight at the Great Pyramid. Churchill, Agatha Christie and Charlie Chaplin stayed here, and the 1977 Mena House Conference helped pave the way to the Camp David Accords. Today it is operated by Marriott.
facts.best_time: October–April, when Cairo’s days are warm rather than scorching.
facts.how_to_get_there: On Pyramids Road in Giza, a few minutes from the plateau’s main gate; Sphinx International Airport is about 30 minutes away and Cairo International about an hour.
facts.good_to_know: Visit the pyramids at opening time to beat the heat and crowds, then retreat to the hotel pool with a pyramid view.

facts.why_go: Bürgenstock has drawn guests since 1873, and after a major rebuild it reopened in 2017 as Switzerland’s largest integrated resort—three hotels, two spas and residences on a ridge high above Lake Lucerne. The Alpine Spa’s infinity pool seems to hang over the lake, and the Hammetschwand Lift, Europe’s highest outdoor elevator, climbs the cliff nearby. Audrey Hepburn married here in 1954.
facts.best_time: May–October for lake cruises and cliff walks; winter brings clear views of snowy peaks.

facts.good_to_know: The Felsenweg cliff path to the Hammetschwand Lift is an easy, spectacular walk.
